## Context
While revalidating `epidemic-chocolaty-imago` at `origin/main` `813baac9b01524a024523a8516d563b17f395358`, `rebar review-plan` failed closed before model execution: `git fetch from origin timed out after 300s`. GitHub authentication and ref discovery were healthy: `git ls-remote --heads origin main` completed in 1.09s.

The code checkout configures `remote.origin.fetch=+refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*`. `rebar._snapshot.repo_snapshot.resolve_ref` always calls `fetch_origin` without a ref before resolution, and materialized attested review sets `blobless=False`; production therefore runs an unfiltered `git fetch origin` across every configured head. This repository deliberately keeps code on `main` and the large ticket store on `tickets` at the same remote, so a review of `origin/main` pulls the unrelated tickets history into the code checkout common object database. At reproduction time that shared database reported 117 packs, 8,758,551 packed objects, and 11.55 GiB of pack storage, plus interrupted temporary packs.

A controlled reproduction of the exact unfiltered general fetch remained active for more than one minute and was stopped after proving the transfer shape. A separate disposable clone configured by `git clone --single-branch --branch main --filter=blob:none` had only `+refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main`, completed in 22 seconds, and the same attested plan review completed with a signed PASS at the exact upstream SHA. This excludes missing credentials, an unreachable remote, ticket material, and the model runner.

## Relationship to existing repairs
`agrologic-oval-bobolink` proves that ref-updating fetches also require common-directory coordination and bounded recovery. Its scope preserves tracker sync’s explicit tickets refspec and addresses concurrent compare-and-swap races; it does not prevent the snapshot layer from fetching unrelated heads or transferring an oversized branch. This bug is complementary, not a duplicate. Do not weaken that ticket’s coordination requirements, remove tracker sync’s explicit tickets refspec, reintroduce a size gate, or make ordinary reviews depend on a tickets-store budget.

## Remediation constraints
Resolve and materialize only the requested gate ref while preserving freshness for moving branches/tags and support for explicit reachable SHAs. An unfiltered materialization may fetch all objects reachable from the selected ref, but must not update or transfer unrelated remote heads. Preserve fail-closed attested semantics, credential-safe errors, noninteractive authentication, partial-clone correctness, and the common-directory coordination/recovery contract tracked by `agrologic-oval-bobolink`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Reviewing `origin/main` against a remote that also has a much larger `tickets` head fetches/materializes `main` without updating `refs/remotes/origin/tickets` or transferring objects reachable only from `tickets`.
- [ ] Moving branch and tag refs are refreshed before resolution, and an explicit reachable SHA remains supported with a descriptive fail-closed error when the server refuses the want.
- [ ] `blobless=False` obtains every blob needed to materialize the selected commit in one bounded path without latching an ordinary clone into an unusable promisor state.
- [ ] Snapshot fetches retain common-Git-directory coordination and bounded recovery from `agrologic-oval-bobolink`; network I/O does not take the ticket write lock.
- [ ] Deterministic local-repository tests include an oversized unrelated branch and prove selected-ref transfer/ref-update isolation before and after the fix.
- [ ] Existing plan-review, completion-verifier, code-review, tag, SHA, partial-clone, authentication, timeout, and narrow-tracker-sync tests remain green.
- [ ] Concurrency/snapshot documentation explains selected-ref fetch scope and its distinction from tracker synchronization.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the project test gate pass.
